messages:
Aisha (CEO): Quick follow-up from today's all-hands on strategy & positioning. I'll answer rapid Qs here. Keep them short.
Priya (sales): Need a crisp 12s reply: "Why Redwood vs building on cloud infra?"
Aisha (CEO): 'We productize inference: predictable latency, transparent unit economics, and deployment choices that meet SLA/compliance needs.' Lead with outcomes, not tech names.
Ken (eng): For demos, any single stat we can memorize that won't age fast?
Tom (VP Product): Use: 'Typical Dedicated customers see ~2x effective token-cost improvement after batching & caching on production workloads.' Cite the benchmark in the sales drive.
Maya (customer-success): One-liner on when to pick Dedicated vs Private?
Aisha (CEO): Dedicated = guaranteed throughput + SLA. Private = data residency/compliance or air-gapped requirements. Start hosted, move when you need isolation.
Priya (sales): Competitor framing: can we say "we replace model ops"?
legal-bot: Suggestion: avoid absolutes. Use 'we reduce the model ops burden by providing runtime primitives (KV cache, rollout controls, optimized kernels) as a managed product.'
Ken (eng): Roadmap push: should infra perf work block new feature launches this sprint?
Aisha (CEO): Short: prioritize infra perf that materially affects paying customers. New features that drive adoption get secondary priority.
Priya (sales): Rebuttal for "we'll self-host" that isn't combative?
Aisha (CEO): 'Many teams underestimate the ongoing reliability and ops cost. We deliver the primitives so your engineers can build product features, not maintain infra.' Keep it respectful.
Tom (VP Product): I'll drop an SLO + battlecard draft in #product in 1h with approved phrasing.
slides-bot: Recording + slides uploaded: https://internal.redwood.example/all-hands/3187654321 :white_check_mark:
Aisha (CEO): Thanks all. If you want to workshop objection handling, ping Tom or me. Closing thread. — Aisha
